How to Get to Sumbawa from Bali and Lombok

  • admin
  • 14 Min Read

articleClasses: post-17778 post type-post status-publish format-standard has-post-thumbnail hentry category-uncategorized
html:
So you’ve set your heart on a Sumbawa trip that has uncrowded waves, hidden waterfalls, and that rare “islands as they used to be” feeling. The only question left is how to actually get here. Sumbawa sits just beyond the well-trodden path of Bali and Lombok, and while reaching it takes a little more planning, that’s exactly what keeps it wonderfully quiet.

Don’t worry, it’s far easier than a glance at the map suggests. In this guide we’ll walk you through every route to West Sumbawa, from the quickest direct flight to the scenic land-and-sea adventure from Bali. And because we love welcoming guests to our corner of the coast, we’ll help you pick the option that suits you best.

Quick Answer: The Fastest Ways to Get to Sumbawa

Where is Sumbawa?

Sumbawa is a large, hilly island in West Nusa Tenggara Province, Indonesia, located directly east of Lombok and Bali. It is the next island in the chain after Lombok, separated from it only by a narrow strait. At their closest point, the two islands are less than nine miles apart, which is why ferries frequently cross there.

The island is much wider than Bali, with two main gateways: Sumbawa Besar in the west and Bima in the east. 

How to Get to Sumbawa

There’s no single “right” way to arrive but it depends on your budget, your timing, and how much of an adventure you’re after. Below we’ve laid out four routes, from the fastest flight to a helicopter splurge, so you can choose your own path to the island.

Option 1: Fly Direct to Sumbawa Besar (SWQ)

If speed and simplicity are your priorities, flying straight to Sumbawa Besar is the most time-efficient way to reach the west coast.

Via Air to Sumbawa Besar

Domestic airlines connect Bali (Denpasar, DPS) and Lombok (LOP) to Sultan Muhammad Kaharuddin III Airport (SWQ) in Sumbawa Besar. There’s typically a daily direct service from Bali. Flights are short and sweet, and they let you skip the ferry crossing entirely. 

Travel to Resort

Sumbawa Besar airport sits right in town, and from there it’s a scenic drive along the coast to our part of West Sumbawa. Rather than wrangling a taxi or bus on arrival, the easiest thing is to let us arrange a private transfer so a friendly driver is waiting when you land.

Option 2: Fly to Lombok, Then Ferry to Poto Tano

Many travellers prefer routing through Lombok, which often has more flight options and connects to Sumbawa via a short sea crossing.

Flights to Lombok

Lombok International Airport (LOP) is well served by domestic flights from Bali and other Indonesian hubs, with plenty of daily departures to choose from. 

By The Sea to Sumbawa

There are a few ways to make the hop, depending on your budget and how quickly you want to arrive.

Ferry

The classic option is the public car ferry from Kayangan (Labuan Lombok) to Poto Tano in West Sumbawa. These run roughly every hour, around the clock, and the crossing takes about one and a half to two hours. They’re affordable and take foot passengers, scooters, and cars. From Poto Tano, it’s a short onward drive to us.

Speed Boat

If you’d rather cut the crossing time, a faster boat service can get you over more quickly and, depending on the option, closer to the west-coast surf areas. Schedules vary and advance booking is wise, so it’s best to confirm current times with us before you travel. 

Private Boat

For the smoothest, most flexible arrival, a private fast boat can take you directly across on your own schedule and, in some cases, drop you close to the beach.

Option 3: Overland from Bali by Ferry

Feeling adventurous? Here’s how it flows, step by step.

Go to Padang Bai

Start on Bali’s east coast at Padang Bai, the harbour town where ferries depart for Lombok. It’s an easy drive from most parts of southern Bali, and a good idea to set off early so the rest of the day runs smoothly.

Ship to Lembar, Lombok

From Padang Bai, board the public ferry across to Lembar Harbour in west Lombok. It’s the longest single leg of the trip (around four to five hours across the strait) so settle in, grab a snack, and enjoy the sea views.

Drive to Kayangan Port

Once you land at Lembar, you’ll travel overland across Lombok to Kayangan (Labuan Lombok) on the east coast. A pre-booked driver makes this leg painless, especially if you’re carrying luggage or boards.

Ship to Poto Tano

From Kayangan, hop on the hourly car ferry across to Poto Tano in West Sumbawa. Aim for a daytime crossing so your onward transfer on the Sumbawa side is easy to arrange.

Poto Tano to Mocean (30 Minutes)

The final stretch from Poto Tano to our coast is a short, pretty drive. Arriving at a quiet port tired and salty is no fun when you’re trying to sort transport on the spot, so let us take the guesswork out of your trip to Sumbawa 

Option 4: Helicopter from Bali

Want to arrive in style? For the ultimate in speed and spectacle, a private helicopter transfer can fly you directly from Bali to West Sumbawa, soaring over Bali, Lombok, and Sumbawa’s dramatic coastlines along the way. 

It’s a premium, seamless choice that turns the journey itself into a highlight. These flights are arranged through specialist providers, and we’re glad to help coordinate one for guests seeking something truly special.

Let Us Book Your Transfer

That’s exactly where we love to help. As your hosts here at Mocean Beach Resort, we can arrange pickups. So, all you have to do is show up and start your holiday.

Tell us where you’re flying from and when you’d like to arrive, and we’ll map out the smoothest route for you.

Send us your flight number or ferry time. We’ll have a driver waiting at Sumbawa Besar airport or Poto Tano port with your name on a sign. Book my transfer on WhatsApp or see transfer details.

Getting to Sumbawa FAQ

What is the easiest way to get to Sumbawa?

The quickest and simplest route is a direct flight from Bali to Sumbawa Besar (SWQ), you can arrive on the same day with minimal fuss. Alternatively, flying to Lombok and taking the ferry to Poto Tano is a popular and scenic choice. Either way, we can arrange your transfers end to end.

Is there a direct ferry from Bali to Sumbawa?

No, there’s no single ferry that goes straight from Bali to Sumbawa. You’ll cross in two stages: first from Bali (Padang Bai) to Lombok (Lembar), then across Lombok to Kayangan for the ferry to Poto Tano in West Sumbawa. Flying to Lombok first lets you skip the long first ferry leg.

Which airport should I choose when visiting West Sumbawa?

For West Sumbawa, choose Sumbawa Besar (SWQ), it’s the closest airport to our coast and the Poto Tano ferry port. Bima (BMU) on the east side is better suited to travellers heading to Lakey Peak or Mount Tambora. If you’re staying with us, SWQ or a flight into Lombok (LOP) followed by the ferry are your best bets.

Can my accommodation help arrange transportation?

Yes and we’d be delighted to. We regularly organise airport transfers, ferry connections, private boats, and helicopter flights for our guests. Just let us know your arrival details and we’ll handle the rest, so your journey to Sumbawa is as smooth and stress-free as possible.
